title: The Day I Became a Team Leader
script: Narrator: [warmly] Last month, my manager called me into her office, and I thought I was in trouble because that almost never happens.
Narrator: Instead, she told me I was going to become the new team leader for the marketing group. I was so surprised that I forgot to say thank you.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I had worked at that company for three years, but I never expected a promotion so soon, especially because two coworkers had been there longer than me.
Narrator: When I told my colleagues, some of them were happy for me, but I could feel that others felt a little strange about it.
Narrator: [carefully] My first week as a leader was harder than I expected, because I had to give tasks to people who used to be my equals.
Narrator: One coworker, Budi, seemed distant at first. He barely spoke to me during meetings, although we used to eat lunch together every day.
Narrator: [reflective] So one afternoon, I asked him directly if something was wrong. He admitted that he had wanted the position too, and he needed some time to accept it.

Narrator: I acknowledged his disappointment without asking him to praise the decision. We discussed his role, my expectations, and how his experience could contribute without making him responsible for my success.
Narrator: [honestly] After that conversation, things slowly improved between us, because we finally spoke honestly instead of avoiding each other.
Narrator: I learned that leadership isn't about being liked immediately. It's about listening carefully, even when a conversation feels uncomfortable.
Narrator: [gently] Now I ask for relevant input, state who decides, use clear criteria, and explain choices. Listening does not remove my responsibility to decide on time.
Narrator: Budi and I have lunch together again, and he recently helped me train a new employee, which meant a lot to me.
Narrator: [encouraging] I document key decisions, invite private and written feedback, and correct mistakes openly. I also ask my manager for coaching when the new authority feels unclear.
Narrator: If someone had told me a year ago that I would lead this team, I probably wouldn't have believed them.
Narrator: [sincere] But here I am, and although it's difficult sometimes, I'm proud of how far I've come since that nervous day in my manager's office.

quiz.question: Why did the narrator think she was in trouble at first?
options: Her manager rarely called her into the office
She had made a big mistake
quiz.explanation: She says her manager almost never calls her in, so she assumed something was wrong.

quiz.question: How did Budi behave toward the narrator during her first week?
options: He seemed distant and barely spoke to her
He asked for a promotion too
quiz.explanation: Budi seemed distant at first, even though they used to eat lunch together.

quiz.question: What did Budi admit when the narrator asked him directly?
options: He had wanted the position too and needed time to accept it
He was moving to another city
quiz.explanation: Budi admitted he had wanted the leadership position and needed time to accept the change.

quiz.question: What does the narrator now do before deciding anything important in meetings?
options: She asks for everyone's opinion first
quiz.explanation: She now asks for everyone's opinion before making important decisions.

quiz.question: What has Budi recently helped the narrator do?
quiz.explanation: Budi recently helped her train a new employee, which meant a lot to her.

quiz.question: Why is Budi distant?
options: He also wanted the leadership role and needs time to adjust
He plans to leave the company
quiz.explanation: His behavior follows an unspoken disappointment.

quiz.question: What should the new leader not ask Budi to do?
options: Praise the selection or hide his disappointment
quiz.explanation: Professional conduct does not require false emotion.

quiz.question: How can the narrator avoid favoritism?
options: Assign work using visible criteria and document important decisions
quiz.explanation: Transparent process matters after promotion among peers.

quiz.question: Why is asking every opinion not the same as shared control?
options: The leader must listen, explain, and still own timely decisions
quiz.explanation: Consultation has a purpose and a responsible decision-maker.

quiz.question: What evidence shows the relationship improves?
options: Budi contributes to training and their work communication becomes normal
quiz.explanation: Cooperation returns without pretending disappointment vanished.
